title: Install PIM Manager (one command)
purpose: Install PIM Manager with one command: download the public PIM Manager release into a new folder, check the download, and run its guided installer (Install-PimManager) with the parameters you give.
whenToRun: Once, to install PIM Manager into your own Azure subscription with only -TenantId and -SubscriptionId. The file decides the edition: the copy from the public GitHub release installs Community; the copy Invardia gives Pro and trial customers installs Pro with the same command (no licence in the command: the installation asks Invardia for its licence by itself). Download it (line 1), then run it with your values (line 2). Run it with -WhatIf first to see the plan; run the same command with -Resume after fixing a stopped step.

runAs.name: Owner
runAs.why: The installer it runs (Install-PimManager) creates the resource group and its resources and assigns Azure roles to the identities it creates (Contributor + User Access Administrator is the equivalent); its check stops before anything is created without it.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: For the installer: Microsoft Graph application permissions for PIM Manager's identities and the SQL admin group. Without it the installation continues and ends with the command for the right person.

runAs.name: Application Administrator
runAs.why: For the installer: the Manager's sign-in app registration (the same as Install-PimManager).

runAs.name: Exchange Administrator (optional)
runAs.why: For the installer: only for the mail sender (a shared mailbox and its scoped send right). Without it the step is a warning with the command for an Exchange Administrator.

runAs.name: Signed in in the browser as yourself (no command-line tool, no PowerShell module, no secret, no certificate)
runAs.scope: the tenant and subscription you name
runAs.why: The installer signs you in in the browser when it first needs Azure or Microsoft Graph. The Community copy itself reads only public release data and needs no sign-in; the Pro copy signs you in in the browser first (an administrator of -TenantId) to download the PIM Manager Pro package from Invardia for that tenant, and hands that sign-in to the installer.

changes.object: a new folder in the temp folder (pim-manager-release-<version>-<random>) with the downloaded release zip and its unpacked files, and a small note (pim-manager-install-<id>.json in the temp folder) with that folder's path so -Resume uses it again
changes.why: The installer runs from the release it was downloaded with; -Resume needs no new download.
changes.undo: Delete the folder and the note.

changes.target: Azure, Microsoft Entra ID, Azure SQL
changes.object: the PIM Manager installation, made by Install-PimManager from the downloaded release (every object, permission and scope is listed on its page: https://invardia.com/docs/pim/scripts/Install-PimManager/)
changes.why: This launcher only fetches the release and starts the installer with your parameters.
changes.undo: As described for Install-PimManager (delete the resource group after exporting the database, and the Entra objects it created).

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The Microsoft Entra tenant PIM Manager manages (passed to Install-PimManager).

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The Azure subscription that hosts PIM Manager (passed to Install-PimManager).

parameters.name: Location
parameters.help: Any Azure region (passed through).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The resource group (passed through).

parameters.name: SuperAdmins
parameters.help: The PIM Manager administrators (passed through).

parameters.name: AlertRecipients
parameters.help: Who gets the alerts (passed through).

parameters.name: MailSender
parameters.help: The mailbox PIM Manager sends from (passed through).

parameters.name: PortalUsers
parameters.help: Who may sign in to PIM Manager (passed through).

parameters.name: AllowAllMembers
parameters.help: Every member account of the tenant may sign in; guests never (passed through).

parameters.name: VnetAddressPrefix
parameters.help: The virtual network range (passed through).

parameters.name: SubnetAddressPrefix
parameters.help: The old name of -AppsSubnetPrefix, kept for one release (passed through).

parameters.name: Exposure
parameters.help: The old switch of the network shape, kept for one release: internal = -PrivateNetwork (passed through).

parameters.name: PrivateNetwork
parameters.help: Install the private shape: no public address (passed through; Install-PimManager's help has the details).

parameters.name: VnetId
parameters.help: A private install: use this existing virtual network (any resource group of the installation's subscription) instead of making one (passed through).

parameters.name: VnetName
parameters.help: The name of the virtual network the installation makes (passed through).

parameters.name: AppsSubnetName
parameters.help: The Container Apps subnet's name (passed through).

parameters.name: AppsSubnetPrefix
parameters.help: The Container Apps subnet's range, a /23 or larger inside the network (passed through).

parameters.name: EndpointsSubnetName
parameters.help: A private install: the private endpoints subnet's name (passed through).

parameters.name: EndpointsSubnetPrefix
parameters.help: A private install: the private endpoints subnet's range, a /28 or larger (passed through).

parameters.name: PrivateDnsZonesResourceGroupId
parameters.help: A private install: your central privatelink zones (a resource group id) -- used, never created or written (passed through).

parameters.name: HubVnetId
parameters.help: A private install: your hub network, for the peering and the zone link (passed through).

parameters.name: LinkZonesToHub
parameters.help: A private install: link PIM Manager's own private zone to the hub (passed through).

parameters.name: PeerToHub
parameters.help: A private install: peer the PIM network with the hub, both sides (passed through).

parameters.name: InternalRanges
parameters.help: A private install behind a hub firewall: the ranges your users connect from, for the app subnet's return route (passed through, with -FirewallIp).

parameters.name: FirewallIp
parameters.help: A private install: your hub firewall's private IP, the return route's next hop (passed through, with -InternalRanges).

parameters.name: WebAppAccess
parameters.help: How the PIM Manager is reached; internal only with -PrivateNetwork, and a private install is always internal (passed through).

parameters.name: UpdateRing
parameters.help: Pro: the update ring, 2 (design partners) or 3 (broad, the default) (passed through).

parameters.name: KeyVaultName
parameters.help: The installation's own Key Vault name (passed through).

parameters.name: EngineAzureRootUserAccessAdmin
parameters.help: Also give the PIM engine User Access Administrator at the tenant root (passed through).

parameters.name: InstallId
parameters.default: derived from tenant, subscription and resource group
parameters.help: The installation id (passed through).

parameters.name: SupportAppId
parameters.help: The Invardia Support app's client id -- only when you want Invardia support to have access (passed through). The Support app is named by its id, never found by name; nothing is granted without it.

parameters.name: SupportAccess
parameters.help: The Support app's level: troubleshoot, setup or asbuilt, used only with -SupportAppId (passed through).

parameters.name: Reporter
parameters.help: Callback that receives every step event (passed through).

parameters.name: StatePath
parameters.help: The installer's resume state folder (passed through).

parameters.name: Resume
parameters.help: Continue a stopped installation: the release downloaded before is used again (passed through).

parameters.name: PreflightOnly
parameters.help: Run only the installer's checks (passed through).

parameters.name: ViaSupportApp
parameters.help: Run the installation as the Invardia Support app (passed through). It needs a Connect-InvardiaSupport session for the same tenant in this PowerShell window; without one it stops before anything is downloaded.

parameters.name: Version
parameters.help: The PIM Manager release to install, for example 3.0.5.

parameters.name: ReleasePath
parameters.help: A folder that already holds the unpacked release: nothing is downloaded.

readsOnly: The public release metadata of the PIM Manager release on GitHub (latest, or -Version) and the release files it names; this file and the release zip are checked against the release before anything runs.

The Pro copy instead: the PIM Manager Pro package of your update ring for your tenant from Invardia (after your browser sign-in) -- Invardia's sealed manifest and the zip it names; that Invardia issued it, the size and the SHA-256 are checked before anything runs. It never falls back to GitHub.
The note in the temp folder that names the release folder of a previous run (-Resume).
network: github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com and release-assets.githubusercontent.com (the release files)
the Pro copy instead: login.microsoftonline.com (the browser sign-in) and invardia.com (the Pro package and the short-lived download link it names)

and everything Install-PimManager reaches (management.azure.com, graph.microsoft.com, login.microsoftonline.com, the database it creates <server>.database.windows.net:1433, the registry it creates <registry>.azurecr.io, outlook.office365.com for the mail sender)
whatIf: Downloads and unpacks the release into a new folder in the temp folder (the plan is read from it), then runs Install-PimManager -WhatIf from it: its checks (reads only) and every step it would take. No note is written and nothing in Azure, Microsoft Entra ID or the database is changed.
undo: Delete the release folder and the note in the temp folder; the installation itself is undone as described for Install-PimManager.
